title: Coredns fails connecting to kube-api via kubernetes service
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

As initially reported [here](https://<redacted-host>/t/coredns-fails-connecting-to-kube-api-via-kubernetes-service/) I'm unable to get dns working due to coredns failing to connect to kubernetes api - I think it might be a regression since upgrading to $latest.

Whole post follows as copy-paste:

### Cluster information:

Kubernetes version: v1.28.1
Cloud being used: bare-metal
Installation method: kubeadm
Host OS: Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS
CNI and version: cilium 1.14.1
CRI and version: containerd 1.6.22

Today, after upgrading to 1.28.1 I realized that my test cluster is unable to get `coredns` ready:

```
$ k get po -A | grep core
kube-system   coredns-5dd5756b68-hchqq            0/1     Running   0             57m
kube-system   coredns-5dd5756b68-r768b            0/1     Running   0             57m
```

Upon inspecting the logs there seem to be some connectivity issue between coredns and kube-api:

```
$ k -n kube-system logs coredns-5dd5756b68-hchqq | tail -5 | tail -2
[WARNING] plugin/kubernetes: Kubernetes API connection failure: Get "https://10.96.0.1:443/version": dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443: i/o timeout
[INFO] plugin/ready: Still waiting on: "kubernetes"
```

```

@reporter There seems to be a regression introduced on participant29 v1.28 that involves app containers getting started before init containers - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120247. 

If you are running with [cgroup v2](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/cgroups/) and cilium socket-lb config enabled, the `mount-cgroup` init container must run prior to the agent. This ensures that the BPF cgroup programs are attached at the right hierarchy. See the kube-proxy replacement guide [1 ](https://<redacted-host>/en/stable/network/kubernetes/kubeproxy-free/#validate-bpf-cgroup-programs-attachment )and [2](https://<redacted-host>/en/stable/installation/kind/#install-cilium) for more details.

As an alternative/workaround, you can mount the cgroup2 fs on the host, see this note in the [guide](https://<redacted-host>/en/stable/network/kubernetes/kubeproxy-free/#quick-start) -   

```
Cilium will automatically mount cgroup v2 filesystem required to attach BPF cgroup programs by participant2 at the path /run/cilium/cgroupv2. To do that, it needs to mount the host /proc inside an init container launched by the DaemonSet temporarily. If you need to disable the auto-mount, specify --set cgroup.autoMount.enabled=false, and set the host mount point where cgroup v2 filesystem is already mounted by using --set cgroup.hostRoot. For example, if not already mounted, you can mount cgroup v2 filesystem by running the below command on the host, and specify --set cgroup.hostRoot=/sys/fs/cgroup.
...

```

/cc @participant8 Which participant29 versions will the regression fix be available in?

For what its worth, I was suffering from this exact same issue and discovered that it wasn't a Cilium issue.

My API server pods were advertising the wrong IP addresses that weren't routable from the other nodes. Look at the `endpoint` resources to see what addresses are backing the Kubernetes API service. I ended up having to change the `--advertise-address` flag in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` to the one I intended to use.
